Nominal pin shear stress with two shear planes: tau = 4T / (pi dp^2 ds)

Hub and shaft hole diameter mismatch no more than 0.05 mm (0.002 in)

Slotted pin primary-retention part at least 60% of overall pin length
Avoid countersinks on the cross hole (longer unsupported pin, more bending)
Key torque is carried on the two flanks; the top face should have clearance
d 6-8 mm: key 2x2, shaft depth t1 1.2, hub depth t2 1.0, key length 6-20 mm
d 17-22 mm: key 6x6, t1 3.5, t2 2.8, length 14-70 mm
d 22-30 mm: key 8x7, t1 4.0, t2 3.3, length 18-90 mm
DIN 6885 key for shaft diameter 30-38 mm: key 10x8, shaft depth t1 5.0, hub depth t2 3.3, length from 22 mm (the 110 mm upper bound was not checked)
DIN 6885 key for shaft diameter 44-50 mm: key 14x9, shaft depth t1 5.5, hub depth t2 3.8, length from 36 mm (the 160 mm upper bound was not checked)
DIN 6885 key for shaft diameter 65-75 mm: key 20x12, shaft depth t1 7.5, hub depth t2 4.9 (the 56-220 mm length range was not checked)
Keyway width fits: tight P9 shaft / P9 hub; normal N9 shaft / JS9 hub; sliding H9 shaft / D10 hub
End-mill keyseat at r/d = 0.02 has Kt about 2.14 in bending and 2.62 in torsion without key; about 3.0 torsion with key fitted
Keep the keyseat end at least d/10 from a shoulder fillet: 0.1 x d
Fatigue notch factor Kf = 1 + q (Kt - 1), q = notch sensitivity; one ASEE paper argues q = 1 should be used for keyseats because q data for them is unverified
Key checks: tangential force Ft = 2 T / d; shear stress = Ft / (b L); bearing stress = Ft / (h_e L), with L the effective key length (design torque with an application factor is a separate step)
Tapered keys are covered by a separate standard, ISO 774
ISO 4026 covers flat-point hexagon socket set screws in metric coarse thread from M1.6 to M24 (2003/2004 edition); the 2026 revision extends steel to M30 and keeps stainless at M24
Cup-point hexagon socket set screws are ISO 4029 (formerly DIN 916); flat-point ones are ISO 4026
Rule of thumb: set screw diameter about half the shaft diameter: 0.5 x shaft diameter
Set screw length about half the shaft diameter in a Shigley-derived design summary: 0.5 x shaft diameter
Design safety factor for set screws: 4 to 8 for dynamic loading, 1.5 to 2.0 static
Two set screws at 90 degrees load more uniformly and hold better than one; tighten sequentially and recheck the first
Supplier installation torques: M3 0.3, M4 0.7, M6 2.5, M8 6.0 N·m (product-specific, not an ISO rating)
